fingerprint_strength_map — IMGFORENSICS sensor op

• Data kinds: fingerprint → image2d

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.fingerprint_strength_map(fingerprint, block: 'int' = 16) -> 'np.ndarray' (to call the implementation directly, import imgforensics; imgforensics.fingerprint_strength_map(fingerprint, block: 'int' = 16) -> 'np.ndarray'; from the registry, opsimgforensics.get("fingerprint_strength_map"))

Usage

A map of the fingerprint's effective strength per block (its standard deviation). image2d.

PRNU does not appear in saturated pixels or pitch-black pixels (it is a multiplicative defect, so it needs signal). This map is for seeing "where the fingerprint can say nothing"; matching results in regions with low values are weak. The standard deviation of each non-overlapping block-square block is returned, expanded back to the original (H, W) as block constants (the edges are filled with the value of the edge block).

Measured (tests/test_imgforensics.py::test_strength_map_marks_the_saturated_half, fingerprint built from 8 images of 128x128 with only the left half saturated): mean strength on the saturated side 0.075 vs. 1.409 on the normal side = 18.8 times. That there is no room for PRNU in the left half (it is a multiplicative defect, so it needs signal) shows up directly.

This is also an exit of the fingerprint vocabulary (so as not to create a dead end).
